svg.title: Candidate CORE table and module execution paths
svg.desc: Static module exports resolve during compilation. A guest field or integer-index instruction operates on the current guest table and key through its table owner. An optional per-instruction slot hint is checked against the current key and value; other accesses follow normal table and metatable rules. Writes, aliases, allocation and collection remain owned by the runtime. The implementation is a candidate, not a measured timing guarantee.
svg.text: CORE — table and module execution candidate
Efficient normal program data, without a module-origin tag or a fixed timing guarantee.

module<const> export

Integer keys: GETI / SETI

General keys: GETT / SETT

Guest indexing and table owner
Integer array and keyed entries · current guest values
Hinted field read: compare the key and check value presence
Otherwise perform the ordinary lookup and metatable operation
Writes use the same owner: aliases observe changes
Deletion, rehash and collection cannot freeze an old result
Metatable effects, errors and ordering remain guest-visible
Other guest values retain their specified indexing rules
Result and execution state
Current value or specified error
Guest registers, PC and frames
Device and interrupt boundaries
Design intent and scope
Common table operations are a normal, efficient workload; C++ / assembly comparison is a design target, not a measured result.
Fast and ordinary paths preserve dynamic guest semantics; hardware allocation, every access latency and all workload costs remain unproven.
Functional proposal only: no new public module representation, mandatory native code format or fabricated silicon is implied.
